Function: Used to check the configuration after generation
Author: Trthinh (Ethan)

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: HyperRAM controller control register. Enables the controller and selects write response, arbitration and request merging.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Resume command. Software writes 1 to leave the hold state after a timeout; hardware clears it when the controller accepts AXI requests again.

Usage: write 1 only while hr_sts.hold = 1, after reading the log (hr_tmo_log, hr_tmo_addr) and, if needed, checking the device with the command port (hr_cmd); a write in any other state is ignored. A software write wins over the hardware clear in the same cycle.

Values:
0x0 no action (reset value);
0x1 leave the hold state; reads 0x1 until the controller has resumed.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Timeout action. Selects what the controller does after a device timeout: stop the failed access and wait for software, or re-initialize the device by itself.

Usage: program it before enable or while idle. With 0 the controller ends the failed access, completes the AXI request with SLVERR, enters the hold state (hr_sts.hold = 1) and holds new AXI requests until software writes hr_ctrl.resume or clears hr_ctrl.en. With 1 it runs the start-up sequence again (RESET# low for t_rp, the waits, CR0, CR1, ID0), completes every queued AXI request with SLVERR, and then accepts requests; the RAM content is lost (REQ-RST-005).

Values:
0x0 abort and wait for software (reset value);
0x1 re-initialize automatically.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Request merging enable. When 1, a request that continues the previous one (same direction, same chip select, next linear address) is sent inside the open HyperBus transaction without a new command and latency phase.

Usage: program it before enable or while idle. Merging stops at the CS#-low limit of the chip select (hr_dN_tcsm.t_csm) and a new transaction starts.

Values:
0x0 every request starts a new HyperBus transaction;
0x1 merge when possible (reset value).

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Posted write mode. Selects when the AXI write response (B channel) is returned: after the data reached the RAM, or as soon as the last write beat is stored in the controller write buffer.

Usage: program it before enable or while the controller is idle; it is applied to writes accepted afterwards. With 1, o_idle stays low until the write buffer is empty, so wait for idle before a reset.

Values:
0x0 B response after the RAM write ended (reset value, safe);
0x1 posted write, B response when the last W beat is buffered.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Controller enable. Starts the start-up sequence of the controller: the RESET# low wait, the device wait times, the CR0 and CR1 writes and the ID0 read, after which AXI requests are accepted.

Usage: program every timing and configuration field of the used chip selects while it is 0, then write 1. Writing 1 while a field is illegal is refused and sets hr_irq_raw.cfg_err. Software writes it; reset clears it. Clearing it later stops the controller and the RAM content is lost.

Values:
0x0 controller disabled, RESET# held low (reset value);
0x1 controller enabled.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: HyperRAM controller status register. Shows the live state of the start-up, the AXI traffic and the device command port.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Hold state flag. Reads 1 while the controller waits for software after a device timeout with hr_ctrl.tmo_act = 0.

Usage: read-only; while it is 1 new AXI requests wait and the device command port still works. Leave it by writing hr_ctrl.resume, or clear hr_ctrl.en to restart with a full start-up.

Values:
0x0 not in hold (reset value);
0x1 hold.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Device command busy. Reads 1 while a device register command started through hr_cmd is running.

Usage: read-only; do not rewrite hr_cmd while it is 1. AXI requests wait while it is 1.

Values:
0x0 no command running;
0x1 command running.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Outstanding writes. Number of accepted AXI writes whose B response has not been delivered yet.

Usage: read-only; with hr_ctrl.wr_posted = 1 the value also counts posted writes still in the buffer.

Values:
0x0 to 0x4 number of outstanding writes.

Unit: writes.

Limits: at most 0x4.

Outstanding reads. Number of accepted AXI reads whose last data beat has not been delivered yet.

Usage: read-only; useful to check that the AXI side is drained.

Values:
0x0 to 0x4 number of outstanding reads.

Unit: reads.

Limits: at most 0x4.

Memory RESET# level. Reads the level driven on the RESET# pin of the HyperRAM (active low).

Usage: read-only; it is 0 while the controller is disabled, in reset or counting hr_dN_trst.t_rp, and 1 after the release.

Values:
0x0 RESET# asserted;
0x1 RESET# released.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Memory power good. Level of the memory power-good input after synchronization to the core clock.

Usage: read-only; a falling edge sets hr_irq_raw.pwr_lost and blocks AXI access until the core reset sequence is run.

Values:
0x0 power not good;
0x1 power good.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Configuration valid. Reads 1 when every timing and configuration field is inside its legal range.

Usage: read-only; check it after programming and before writing hr_ctrl.en. When it is 0 the enable is refused and hr_irq_raw.cfg_err is set.

Values:
0x0 at least one field is illegal;
0x1 all fields are legal.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Controller idle. Same condition as the o_idle output: all accepted work is finished, the write buffer is empty, no command runs and CS# is high.

Usage: read-only; the SoC reset logic waits for 1 before it asserts the core reset (the APB side stays out of this wait).

Values:
0x0 busy or not initialized;
0x1 idle.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Initialization done. Reads 1 when the start-up sequence has completed and the controller accepts AXI requests and device commands.

Usage: read-only; wait for 1 before any AXI access or hr_cmd command. A core reset or clearing hr_ctrl.en returns it to 0.

Values:
0x0 not ready;
0x1 ready.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Start-up busy. Reads 1 while the controller runs the RESET#, wait, CR0, CR1 and ID0 sequence after enable.

Usage: read-only; poll it after writing hr_ctrl.en. It falls to 0 when hr_sts.init_done rises.

Values:
0x0 not running;
0x1 start-up running.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: HyperRAM controller capability register. Reports the elaboration parameters of this build.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Delay-line select width. Reports the width of the delay-line tap select, PARA_DLY_TAP_W.

Usage: read-only; the field hr_dN_rcap.tap uses only this many low bits.

Values:
0x1 to 0x8 width of the delay-line tap select.

Unit: bits.

Limits: none.

Number of chip selects. Reports the parameter PARA_NUM_CS.

Usage: read-only; program the register group hr_d1_* only when it is 2.

Values:
0x1 one chip select;
0x2 two chip selects.

Unit: chip selects.

Limits: 0x1 or 0x2.

Memory width. Reports the HyperBus profile chosen with the parameter PARA_MEM_DQ_W.

Usage: read-only; select the device values that match this width.

Values:
0x0 x8 HyperBus;
0x1 x16 Extended-I/O.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

AXI data width. Reports the width chosen with the parameter PARA_AXI_DATA_W.

Usage: read-only; software uses it to size its AXI accesses.

Values:
0x0 32-bit AXI data;
0x1 64-bit AXI data.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: HyperRAM aperture size register. Reports the byte capacity of one chip select.

Bits.Description:
Aperture size of one chip select. Reports the parameter PARA_MEM_SIZE_BYTES, the size of the AXI address window that maps to one device.

Usage: read-only; the second chip select starts at this offset in the AXI window.

Values:
0x00000001 to 0x02000000 aperture size of one chip select (reset value 0x02000000, that is 32 MiB).

Unit: bytes.

Limits: not larger than the device capacity.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: HyperBus clock register. Sets the clock divider, the clock type and the clock phase of the memory interface.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

CK phase select. Chooses the core clock edge on which CK toggles, which sets the offset between CK and the write data.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0. With 0 the CK edge lies in the middle of each write data interval (1.25 ns from the data change at 200 MHz); with 1 CK and data change on the same edge.

Values:
0x0 CK toggles on the falling core clock edge (reset value);
0x1 CK toggles on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Differential clock enable. Selects whether the controller drives the complementary clock CK# or leaves it high; it is also written into CR1[6] of the device.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0, before the start-up writes CR1; the devices must support the chosen clock type.

Values:
0x0 single-ended CK, CK# held high (reset value);
0x1 differential CK and CK#.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

HyperBus clock divider. Number of core clock cycles in one HyperBus CK period; CK is the core clock divided by this value.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0 and rescale every timing count (they are counted in CK periods) when you change it. 2 gives CK = 200 MHz for a 400 MHz core clock.

Values:
0x02 to 0xFE even values only (reset value 0x02);
0x03 to 0xFD odd values are illegal; 0x00 and 0x01 are illegal.

Unit: core clock cycles per CK period.

Limits: odd values, 0x00 and 0x01 are illegal (cfg_valid = 0); the CK frequency must not exceed 200 MHz.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Device register command register. Starts a read or a write of one register of the HyperRAM device.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Command chip select. Selects the chip select (device) that receives the command.

Usage: program it before writing hr_cmd.go; value 1 is legal only when hr_cap.num_cs is 2.

Values:
0x0 chip select 0;
0x1 chip select 1.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Command direction. Selects whether the command reads or writes the device register.

Usage: program it before writing hr_cmd.go. A write sends hr_cmd_wdata with zero latency; a read waits the programmed latency and captures one word into hr_cmd_rdata.rdata.

Values:
0x0 read the register;
0x1 write the register.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Command start. Starting bit of a device register command; hardware clears it when the command has finished.

Usage: first write hr_cmd_addr, hr_cmd_wdata (for a write), hr_cmd.wr and hr_cmd.cs, then write 1 here, only when hr_sts.cmd_busy = 0. A software write wins over the hardware clear in the same cycle, so do not rewrite the register while the command runs.

Values:
0x0 no command running (reset value);
0x1 start the command; reads 0x1 until the command is done.

Unit: none.

Limits: a command before hr_sts.init_done = 1 is rejected and sets hr_cmd_rdata.err.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Device register address register. Holds the address of the device register for a command.

Bits.Description:
Device register address. Word address sent in the command and address phase with the register-space bit set.

Usage: program it before writing hr_cmd.go; the register addresses (for example ID0, ID1, CR0 and CR1) are given in the device datasheet.

Values:
0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF word address of the device register space.

Unit: 16-bit words.

Limits: use only addresses that the device defines.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Device register write data register. Holds the data of a device register write command.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Device register write data. The 16-bit value written into the device register by a write command.

Usage: program it before writing hr_cmd.go with hr_cmd.wr = 1; unused for a read command.

Values:
0x0000 to 0xFFFF data of the register write.

Unit: none.

Limits: write reserved device fields with their default value; writing CR0[7:4] differently from hr_dN_cfg.init_lat sets hr_irq_raw.lat_mis.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Device register read data register. Returns the data of a device register read command and its completion flags.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Command error flag. Hardware sets it when a command is rejected because the controller is not initialized.

Usage: check it when hr_cmd_rdata.done does not rise; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no error;
0x1 command rejected.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Command done flag. Hardware sets it when a device register command has completed; software clears it.

Usage: poll it or use hr_irq_raw.cmd_done; write 1 to clear before the next command. A hardware set in the same cycle as the clear wins.

Values:
0x0 no completed command;
0x1 command completed.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Device register read data. The 16-bit word captured by the last read command.

Usage: read it after hr_cmd_rdata.done is 1; its content is not defined before.

Values:
0x0000 to 0xFFFF content of the device register.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Raw interrupt status register. Holds the sticky event flags of the controller before masking.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Device timeout event. Set when the device did not answer within the wait time of hr_dN_tmo.t_tmo, for example no read data strobe after the initial latency.

Usage: read hr_tmo_log and hr_tmo_addr to find the command, the address and the step that was waited for; then act as hr_ctrl.tmo_act selects; write 1 to clear. The log stays until hr_tmo_log.valid is cleared.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Device command done event. Set when a device register command has completed.

Usage: together with hr_cmd_rdata.done; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Latency mismatch event. Set when a device register write changes CR0[7:4] to a latency code that differs from hr_dN_cfg.init_lat.

Usage: the controller keeps its own latency; restore CR0 or change init_lat while disabled; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

ID mismatch event. Set when the ID0 value read after start-up differs from hr_dN_id.id0_exp of that chip select.

Usage: only active when hr_dN_id.id_chk_en = 1; AXI access is not blocked; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Power loss event. Set when the synchronized memory power-good signal falls.

Usage: run the reset sequence of the SoC; accepted work may not complete; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

AXI slave error event. Set when a request with an unsupported burst type (FIXED) is answered with SLVERR.

Usage: details are in hr_err_ri and hr_err_wi; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

AXI decode error event. Set when a request addresses bytes outside the aperture and is answered with DECERR.

Usage: the address and ID of the request are in hr_err_ra and hr_err_wa; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Configuration error event. Set when hr_ctrl.en is written with an illegal field, or when a CSR field is changed in a way that the controller refuses.

Usage: read hr_sts.cfg_valid to find that a field is illegal; correct the field and write hr_ctrl.en again; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Initialization complete event. Set when the start-up sequence has finished.

Usage: enable it in hr_irq_en to get an interrupt instead of polling hr_sts.init_done; write 1 to clear.

Values:
0x0 no event;
0x1 event occurred.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Interrupt injection register. Lets software raise raw interrupt events for test.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Device timeout injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the device timeout event of hr_irq_raw once, as if the device did not answer within the programmed wait time.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Device command done injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the device command done event of hr_irq_raw once, as if a device register command has completed.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Latency mismatch injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the latency mismatch event of hr_irq_raw once, as if a device register write changes the CR0 latency code to a value that differs from init_lat.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

ID mismatch injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the id mismatch event of hr_irq_raw once, as if the ID0 read after start-up differs from the expected value.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Power loss injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the power loss event of hr_irq_raw once, as if the synchronized memory power-good signal falls.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

AXI slave error injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the axi slave error event of hr_irq_raw once, as if a request is answered with SLVERR.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

AXI decode error injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the axi decode error event of hr_irq_raw once, as if a request is answered with DECERR.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Configuration error injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the configuration error event of hr_irq_raw once, as if hr_ctrl.en is written with an illegal field.

Usage: write 1 to inject and write 0 before the next injection, because only the rising edge counts; use it with hr_irq_en to test the interrupt path and its handler. The raw event is then cleared in hr_irq_raw as for a real event.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject on the rising edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Initialization complete injection. A rising edge from 0 to 1 raises the initialization complete event of hr_irq_raw once, as if the start-up sequence has finished.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: AXI error counter register. Counts the AXI requests answered with an error.

Bits.Description:

Values:

Unit: requests.

Limits: saturating, no clear by software.

DECERR counter. Number of AXI requests answered with DECERR since the last core reset; saturates at the maximum.

Usage: read-only; compare with hr_irq_raw.decerr.

Values:
0x0000 to 0xFFFF number of rejected requests, saturating.

Unit: requests.

Limits: saturating, no clear by software.

Usage: valid only when the valid bit of hr_err_ri is 1; it is overwritten by the next error.

Values:
0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF byte address relative to the aperture window.

Unit: bytes.

Limits: none.

0x1 captured.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Usage: valid only when hr_err_ri.valid is 1.

Values:
0x2 SLVERR;
0x3 DECERR.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Timeout log register. Holds what the controller was doing and waiting for when the last device timeout happened.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Completed words. Number of 16-bit words transferred in the failed transaction before the timeout.

Usage: read-only; valid only while valid = 1; with hr_tmo_addr it gives the failing position inside a burst.

Values:
0x0000 to 0x1FFF number of completed 16-bit words, saturating.

Unit: 16-bit words.

Limits: counts up to 8191.

Timed-out direction. Direction of the command that timed out.

Usage: read-only; valid only while valid = 1.

Values:
0x0 read;
0x1 write.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Timed-out chip select. The chip select (device) that did not answer.

Usage: read-only; valid only while valid = 1.

Values:
0x0 chip select 0;
0x1 chip select 1.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Log valid flag. Hardware sets it with the first timeout and the log registers then keep their values; software clears it to arm the next capture.

Usage: read the log (hr_tmo_log and hr_tmo_addr) after hr_irq_raw.tmo is set, then write 1 here. A second timeout while it is 1 does not overwrite the log. A hardware set in the same cycle as the clear wins.

Values:
0x0 no log captured (reset value);
0x1 log captured.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Timeout address register. Holds the address of the transaction that timed out.

Bits.Description:
Timed-out address. Byte address, relative to the aperture window, of the first byte of the transaction that timed out; for a device register command it is the register word address.

Usage: read-only; valid only while hr_tmo_log.valid = 1.

Values:
0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF byte address relative to the aperture window.

Unit: bytes.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 device configuration register. Holds the latency and mode values written to the device.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Partial array refresh code. Value written into CR1[4:2] to choose which part of the array is refreshed.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; the data outside the refreshed part is lost.

Values:
0x0 full array (reset value);
0x1 to 0x7 other codes per the device datasheet.

Unit: code.

Limits: none.

Hybrid burst control. Value written into CR0[2], which selects how a wrapped burst continues after the wrap group.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; it matters only for wrapped bursts of the devices that support hybrid burst.

Values:
0x0 hybrid burst as defined by the device;
0x1 legacy wrapped burst (reset value).

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Output drive strength code. Value written into CR0[14:12] to set the output impedance of the DQ and RWDS drivers of the device.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; choose it for the board; the code meaning is given in the device datasheet.

Values:
0x0 to 0x7 drive strength code (reset value 0x0, 34 ohm on the target devices).

Unit: code.

Limits: some codes duplicate another code on some devices.

Fixed latency enable. Selects whether the latency is always twice the initial latency or follows RWDS in the command and address phase; written into CR0[3].

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0 together with init_lat. In variable mode the controller samples RWDS during the CA phase and waits 1x or 2x init_lat.

Values:
0x0 variable latency (RWDS decides);
0x1 fixed latency of 2 x init_lat (reset value).

Unit: none.

Limits: use 0x0 only with devices that support variable latency.

Initial latency. Number of CK periods the controller waits between the command and address phase and the first data; the controller encodes it into CR0[7:4] at start-up.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; with fixed latency the wait is twice this value. Keep it equal to the latency code in the device CR0, otherwise hr_irq_raw.lat_mis is set when CR0 is changed by software.

Values:
0x03 to 0x08 number of CK periods (reset value 0x07, correct for a 200 MHz CK);
0x08 exists only on devices that support it.

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: values outside 0x03 to 0x08 are illegal (cfg_valid = 0); the value must be correct for the CK frequency.

This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 RESET# timing register. Sets the RESET# low time and the wait after RESET# is released.

Bits.Description:
RESET# high to CS# low time. Number of CK periods the controller waits after RESET# is released before CS# may go low.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; it must cover the device tRH (200 ns on the target devices).

Values:
0x0000 illegal;
0x0001 to 0xFFFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x0050, that is 400 ns at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal; rescale it when hr_clk.ck_div changes.

RESET# pulse width. Number of CK periods the controller holds RESET# low at start-up.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; with two chip selects the larger value of both groups is used; it must cover the device tRP (200 ns on the target devices).

Values:
0x0000 illegal;
0x0001 to 0xFFFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x0050, that is 400 ns at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal; rescale it when hr_clk.ck_div changes.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 RESET# low to CS# low register. Sets the wait from the start of RESET# to the first access.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

RESET# low to CS# low time. Number of CK periods from the start of RESET# low to the first CS# low.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; it must cover the device tRPH (400 ns on the target devices).

Values:
0x0000 illegal;
0x0001 to 0xFFFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x00A0, that is 800 ns at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal; rescale it when hr_clk.ck_div changes.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 power-up time register. Sets the wait before the first access after power-up.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Power-up wait. Number of CK periods from VCC valid and RESET# high to the first access (device tVCS).

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; it must cover the device tVCS (150 us on the target devices).

Values:
0x0000 illegal;
0x0001 to 0xFFFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x9C40, that is 200 us at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal; at a low CK frequency the maximum covers a shorter time, so check it.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 minimum wait register. Sets the minimum CS# high time, read-write recovery and CS# setup.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

CS# setup time. Number of CK periods between CS# going low and the first CK edge (device tCSS).

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; the target devices need 3 to 4 ns.

Values:
0x00 illegal;
0x01 to 0xFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x02, that is 10 ns at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal.

Read-write recovery time. Minimum number of CK periods from the CS# rising edge of one transaction to the end of the CA1 phase of the next transaction to the same device (device tRWR).

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; it sets the real gap between two transactions together with t_cshi.

Values:
0x00 illegal;
0x01 to 0xFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x07, that is 35 ns at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal.

CS# high time. Minimum number of CK periods that CS# stays high between two transactions to this device (device tCSHI).

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; the target devices need 6 ns or less.

Values:
0x00 illegal;
0x01 to 0xFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x02, that is 10 ns at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0 is illegal.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 CS# low limit register. Sets the longest time CS# may stay low.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

CS# low limit. Maximum number of CK periods from CS# low to CS# high, including the command, latency and data phases; the controller splits longer transfers (device tCSM).

Usage: set it for the device and its operating temperature (1 us above 85 C on some devices, 4 us otherwise); a larger value gives fewer transaction restarts and higher throughput.

Values:
0x0000 and 0x0321 to 0xFFFF illegal;
0x0001 to 0x0320 number of CK periods (reset value 0x00A0, that is 1 us at 200 MHz; 0x0320 is 4 us).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: 0x0000 and values above 0x0320 are illegal; the device limit must not be exceeded.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 read capture register. Sets the delay-line tap used to capture read data.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Delay-line tap. Code sent to the external delay line that delays RWDS so that its edges fall in the middle of the read data of this device.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0 and tune it on the board; it is applied between transactions. Only the low hr_cap.dly_w bits are used.

Values:
0x00 to the maximum tap of the delay line (reset value 0x00).

Unit: delay-line steps (technology specific).

Limits: the useful range depends on the delay line and on hr_clk.ck_div.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 device ID check register. Holds the expected device ID and enables the check.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

ID check enable. Enables the comparison of the device ID0 with id0_exp after start-up.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; a mismatch sets hr_irq_raw.id_mis and does not block AXI access.

Values:
0x0 no check (reset value);
0x1 check ID0.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Expected ID0 value. The value that the controller compares with the ID0 register of the device after start-up.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; it is used only when id_chk_en = 1.

Values:
0x0000 no expected value (reset value);
0x0001 to 0xFFFF ID0 of the device.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 timeout register. Sets the longest time the controller waits for the device in one step.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Device wait time. Maximum number of CK periods the controller waits for one answer of the device (read data strobe after the initial latency, next strobe edge in a burst) before it declares a timeout.

Usage: program it while hr_ctrl.en = 0; the action after a timeout is chosen by hr_ctrl.tmo_act. The value must be longer than the longest legal wait of the device (initial latency 2 x init_lat plus refresh) so that no healthy access times out.

Values:
0x0000 timeout disabled;
0x0001 to 0x000F illegal;
0x0010 to 0xFFFF number of CK periods (reset value 0x0200, that is 2.56 us at 200 MHz).

Unit: CK periods.

Limits: values 1 to 15 are illegal (cfg_valid = 0); rescale it when hr_clk.ck_div changes.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Chip select 0 device ID0 register. Holds the ID0 value that the controller read from the device at start-up.

Bits.Description:

Usage: read-only; valid after hr_sts.init_done = 1; compare it with the datasheet of the device, or read ID0 again at any time through the device command port (hr_cmd with the ID0 register address in hr_cmd_addr).

Values:
0x0000 to 0xFFFF ID0 value read from the device.

Unit: none.

Limits: 0x0000 before the start-up read.
